serving.text_only_input_quote: messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "Describe the mechanism of action of metformin."}]
serving.notes: config.json max_position_embeddings is 40960 and torch_dtype is float16; the Hub safetensors metadata reports 8,190,735,360 BF16 parameters. The chat template inserts a system turn only when the caller supplies one. The card example uses max_new_tokens=300. This repo has four full weight shards and no adapter_config.json. Rank 32 and alpha 32 are in the sibling adapter at https://huggingface.co/Satyam810/qwen3-8b-medical-reasoning-lora/raw/main/adapter_config.json (r 32, lora_alpha 32, base unsloth/Qwen3-8B-unsloth-bnb-4bit). The card's Unsloth link is the training library, not a script for this checkpoint. The English medical-o1 config has 19,704 rows and the dataset has 90,120 rows across four configs; the card says training used a shuffled subsample of 7,000 combined examples and does not name the config.

evaluation_reported.text: Fine-tuning didn't change diagnostic correctness on this small test set — both the base and fine-tuned model reached the same correct diagnosis on all five test questions. What changed was response style: the fine-tuned model consistently produced shorter, more conversational answers (avg. ~35% fewer words across three of five test questions). The card says this has not been evaluated against standard medical benchmarks (e.g. MedQA).

discrepancies: Inventory methods is lora. The card trains LoRA rank 32 on the 4-bit checkpoint unsloth/Qwen3-8B-unsloth-bnb-4bit, which is QLoRA, then this repository stores full BF16 weights. Inventory parent Qwen/Qwen3-8B matches the YAML base_model only. The training sentence and the sibling adapter config name unsloth/Qwen3-8B-unsloth-bnb-4bit. Datasets match the inventory row. The card does not state learning rate, batch size, or step count.
